$comment:
Four notes.

**It is `kind: gameplay`, and that is not a fudge.** The split is a *data direction*: a `hud` mod owns a draggable item this client draws and places, a `gameplay` mod mutates something the game was going to do anyway. This mod draws nothing — every pixel of the sidebar is vanilla's, and all four settings change how vanilla's own draw is set up. It is the same shape as `overlay`, which is a grab-bag of suppressions of things the game draws, and the same reason `crosshair` and `hitboxes` carry their own geometry without being HUD items: that geometry belongs to a mark the *world* pass draws.

**Why it is not a HUD item, when a HUD editor exists.** `docs/mod-roster.md` §3.1 #16 already answers this for the boss bar and the titles: vanilla overlays become HUD items "only once the HUD editor can own vanilla elements", which it cannot — `loadout.json`'s `hud[]` is a list of *this client's* widgets, and the editor's drag writes an anchor and an offset that `HudSlot` applies to a React box. There is no React box here. Giving the scoreboard `offset_y` as a row rather than a drag handle is the honest version of that limitation, and the day the editor learns to place a vanilla element this mod becomes its first caller.

**Scale is about the right edge, because that is where the sidebar is anchored.** Read out of `InGameHud.renderScoreboardObjective` rather than assumed: at offsets 221-231 the left edge is `window.getWidth() - maxWidth - 3`, and at 205-216 the top is `window.getHeight() / 2 + rows * fontHeight / 3`. So the sidebar grows leftwards and downwards from a point on the right edge at half height, and a scale about the origin would slide it into the middle of the screen. The transform anchors that point.

**No recolouring.** Lunar's version recolours the sidebar's text and its ground. `design/quiet-cell-system.md` §1 rules a per-element colour out, and here it is not even our colour to choose: the server writes those colour codes and they carry meaning in every game mode that uses them. Hiding the whole thing is a choice; repainting a server's own message is not.

**The glyph is `users`, not `list`.** A scoreboard is a list, and `list` is the mark that reads it — but that mark is one of the overlay bar's own four controls, three inches above the grid and on screen at the same time, so a tile carrying it would be a tile that looks like a button. `users` is unused by any mod and is honest about the content: a sidebar is players and their scores. The three glyph *shares* in this registry are all pairs of mods reading one subject; borrowing a chrome control is a different thing and is not one of them.

**`scale` is spelled `sidebar_scale`, and the generator is why.** `SETTING_BOUNDS` is keyed by the bare setting name and throws if two mods disagree about a bound, which is the right rule: `scale` is the shared HUD block's, 0.25 to 4, and this wants 0.5 to 1.5 because vanilla's font is a bitmap that stops resolving below half size. `ModSettingsScreen`'s `SPATIAL_KEYS` is the second reason — it puts anything called `scale` or `size` on the preview as a drag handle, and this mod's preview is a diagram with nothing to drag.
label: Scoreboard
description: Hide, shrink or move the server's sidebar, which vanilla nails to the right of the screen.
settings_description:
Settings for the Scoreboard gameplay mod. It draws nothing of its own: every pixel is vanilla's `InGameHud.renderScoreboardObjective`, and this changes whether that runs and what transform it runs under.

Why it is worth a mod at all — `docs/mod-roster.md` §3.1 #7: the vanilla sidebar covers the right third of the screen, at a size chosen for a 2011 resolution, and on most servers it is a scoreboard you have already read. It is also exactly where a right-handed player's eye goes for their own HUD.

The geometry was read out of the method rather than remembered. The sidebar's left edge is `window.getWidth() - maxWidth - 3` and its top is `window.getHeight() / 2 + rows * fontHeight / 3`, so it hangs from a point on the right edge at half height and grows left and down from there. `scale` is applied about that point, which is why shrinking it keeps it in its corner instead of sliding it into the middle of the screen.

hide.description: Whether the sidebar is drawn at all. Off by default, because a scoreboard is the only thing telling you the score in half the game modes it appears in and a mod that ships hiding it would be a mod that breaks Bedwars for anyone who enables it without reading. On, nothing is drawn — the whole method is skipped, so it costs less than vanilla rather than more.

sidebar_scale.description: Size of the sidebar, as a multiplier on vanilla's. 1 is untouched. Applied about the sidebar's own anchor — the point on the right edge at half height that the method hangs it from — so shrinking it keeps it in its corner rather than sliding it towards the middle. The floor is 0.5 because vanilla's font is a bitmap: below half size the glyphs stop resolving into letters, and a scoreboard nobody can read is `hide` with extra steps.

offset_x.description: Horizontal nudge in scaled screen pixels, positive to the right. The useful direction is negative — pulling the sidebar in off the edge — but both are offered because a player who has shrunk it may want it flush again.

offset_y.description:
Vertical nudge in scaled screen pixels, positive downwards. This is the setting most players actually want: the sidebar sits at half height, which on a 16:9 screen is straight through the middle of a fight, and moving it up puts it above the horizon where a bow arc lives instead.

It is a row rather than a drag handle on a preview, and that is a stated limitation rather than an oversight — see this mod's `$comment`. The HUD editor places *this client's* widgets, and every pixel here is vanilla's.
